title: Making Du'a Together: Teaching the Heart to Cling to Allah
summary: Du'a is the simplest and deepest thing you can teach your child at this age: that Allah has a door always open. Teach him short, easy du'a for their contexts (before eating, at bedtime, when afraid), and let him make du'a in his own words sometimes, even in colloquial speech. When he sees that du'a brings calm and reassurance, his heart will cling to Allah with a living relationship, not dry memorisation. Make du'a in front of him for him and for others, so he learns that du'a encompasses others. The child who grows accustomed to du'a early carries in his heart the certainty that he is not alone, and that he has a Lord who is near and hears him—this is the deepest psychological and spiritual security.
try_this: This week: Choose a daily moment (like bedtime) and make du'a together with a short du'a, then let your child add a du'a in his own words. Notice if he begins to make du'a spontaneously.
reflection_prompts: How can you make du'a a warm, reassuring moment for your child, not a duty to be performed?
What does your child learn about Allah when he sees you making du'a with confidence and tranquility?
